sermon.title: Adding Patience
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this seventh session on Bible morality, the speaker says patience must be added to self-control, knowledge, goodness and faith, defining it as the ability to wait and relax during provocation, annoyance, misfortune, delays and pain. He shows patience in relationships (Romans 15:4–5), in bearing fruit (Luke 8:15), in persecution (Luke 21), in choosing whom to imitate (Hebrews 6:12) and in testing and temptation (James 1, Hebrews 4:15).
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The speaker is not named in the recording; it is the seventh session (“In the seventh session”) of the Bible morality series that continues “Adding Knowledge” and “Adding Self-Control,” which were also attributed to Pastor David G. Kincer, so Michael should confirm. He reads from a translation other than the NKJV (for example, Hebrews 6:12 “do not become lazy”), so the NKJV shown differs in wording. “James tells us the faith without actions is dead” is quoted without a verse (James 2:17 is shown). Caption corrections: “in personal relationships,” “humanists and their followers,” “Humanism promotes,” and “in persecution”; one word after “they took the” is [unclear]. Sensitive content, kept as spoken: he says humanists, free thinkers, liberals, hedonists, atheists, religionists, environmentalists and homosexual activists hate the Bible and Jesus, that public schools teach children their Bible-believing parents are idiots, and that humanists promote moral crimes.
